acquisition-acquisition:ashbyhq:5a24111e.title: Senior Director, Finance
acquisition-acquisition:ashbyhq:5a24111e.description: ROLE The Senior Director of Finance exists to own the quality of planning, the integrity of numbers, and the clarity of reporting that Acquisition.com http://Acquisition.com's leaders run the business on. Acquisition.com http://Acquisition.com is a multi-line, portfolio-backed business that scales its finance function through systems and automation rather than headcount. The challenge is not complexity for its own sake. The challenge is building a finance organization that delivers trusted numbers, audit-ready operations, and decision-grade reporting while staying deliberately lean. This is a player-coach role. You will build the model, run the analysis, and get into the numbers yourself while developing the leaders beneath you. Beyond the core function, you provide financial oversight across a portfolio of investments and outsourced partner relationships, and you serve as a thought partner to the President and CFO on capital allocation and tax strategy. You report to the President and CFO and lead a small, high-leverage finance team. RESPONSIBILITIES - Own budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning that leadership actually steers by, and the reporting architecture that makes the business legible from the executive level down to each unit's economics. - Run a clean, compliant, audit-ready accounting function: GAAP close, revenue recognition, consolidations, financial operations, and a successful first external audit. - Serve as the finance partner to operating businesses, bringing rigor to unit economics and performance where the company creates its value. - Oversee liquidity, financing relationships, the investment portfolio, and outsourced partner interfaces; recommend and execute on capital allocation and tax strategy in partnership with the President and CFO. - Set the target state for the finance technology stack and data environment, and drive the function toward it. - Lead a deliberately lean finance organization, developing direct reports into stronger operators and multiplying capability through systems, automation, and standards rather than headcount. REQUIREMENTS - Proven ownership of FP&A and the reporting architecture in a multi-entity environment, with plans and forecasts that leadership actually used to run the business. - Led a finance function through a GAAP close and external audit, including revenue recognition, consolidations, and the controls framework that makes them defensible. - Experience as a hands-on finance partner to operating businesses, with demonstrated ability to sharpen unit economics and drive performance at the business-unit level. - Judgment that travels: the ability to oversee investments, liquidity, and partner relationships without running them, and to turn analysis into capital allocation decisions for executive audiences. - Track record of modernizing or building a finance technology stack and using systems and automation to increase the function's capability. - 12+ years of progressive finance leadership, including direct management of finance leaders across multiple disciplines, with a player-coach disposition: equally credible building the model yourself and leading the people who will. CPA, CFA, or MBA preferred. RESULTS - Plans, forecasts, and financials are accurate, on time, and actively used to run the business. - The company completes its external audit with strong controls, documentation, and governance across all entities. - Liquidity, financing, and the portfolio are managed proactively, and capital allocation recommendations are well-modeled and cleanly executed. - Leadership and every business unit see the numbers that matter, on a cadence they can count on. - The finance function's capability grows with the business through systems, automation, and leverage, not headcount, and its leaders grow faster than their roles. SCHEDULE - Standard business hours with flexibility to support close cycles, audit periods, and executive planning cadences. LOCATION - Remote, USA CO

foundersfactory-founders-factory:ashbyhq.description: 👋 HEY, WE'RE FOUNDERS FACTORY Founders Factory builds and funds startups together with exceptional entrepreneurs and the world's leading companies. Headquartered in London and operating globally, Founders Factory backs visionary founders with capital, dedicated support from a team of expert operators, and unrivalled access to a coalition of industry leading corporate partners. Since 2015, FF has backed 450+ portfolio companies helping them to secure over 500 enterprise pilots with blue chip corporate partners such as Aviva, Northwestern Medicine, Johnson & Johnson Innovation, and HSBC. The Opportunity: Health systems globally are burdened by capacity constraints, rising chronic disease, aging populations, and escalating operational costs. Care delivery models built around physical hospitals are increasingly unsustainable. Advances in connected devices, remote diagnostics, and AI-enabled monitoring now make it possible to safely move large parts of care beyond hospital walls while improving outcomes and patient experience. The big promise of technology in this space is to enable continuous, proactive, and lower cost care particularly across long-term condition management or home-based / community care while allowing scarce clinical resources to focus where they matter most. We are looking for exceptional Venture Builders who are passionate about building the future of healthcare delivery. 🔍 WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? As a Venture Builder, you specialise in taking ideas from zero to venture-backable businesses. You work closely with founders to shape strategy, validate problem spaces, build MVPs, and find early product market fit. This is a hands on, high ownership role. You’ll operate across product, design, growth and tech, moving fast, making decisions, and focusing relentlessly on what creates the most leverage at each stage of a venture. You have a varied skill set and will have demonstrated an interest in tech and entrepreneurship. You will be an advocate for FF’s values and mission and be committed to supporting founders. You are opinionated but evidence led, creative but commercial, and comfortable operating in ambiguity. You care deeply about building products people actually want and businesses that can scale. Please note that we are looking for someone who is available for an initial 6 month contract with possible extension or full-time employment. 💪 Your responsibilities: - Owning the end-to-end early build: from problem definition and MVP scoping through to shipping, testing, and iteration - Getting products into users hands fast, using lean, experimental approaches to validate assumptions and generate learning - Shaping the customer experience and product vision, balancing user needs with commercial and technical realities - Working closely with founders to challenge thinking, sharpen focus, and drive momentum, especially when things feel unclear or uncomfortable - Helping ventures progress through studio stage gates, supporting founders towards strong, evidence-backed IC decisions - Spotting opportunities early by staying close to market dynamics, emerging tech, and real user behaviour - Communicating clearly and regularly, sharing progress, learnings, trade-offs, and recommendations with founders and the wider studio 🎯 REQUIRED SKILLS, EXPERIENCE AND MINDSET: - Demonstrated 0→1 experience in digital health or medtech, whether at a startup, through a side project, research, or volunteering (experience applying AI or developing innovative health/medical devices are considered highly advantageous). - Driving momentum by subscribing to lean methodologies and an experimental approach, you prioritise speed, learning, and focus over perfection - Comfortable wearing multiple hats (product, design, tech, growth) and knowing when to pull in specialist support - Strong technical mindset, with the ability to build no-code / low-code solutions, prototypes, or proofs of concept to accelerate validation - Commercially curious with

getwingapp-getwingapp:lever:b06a6db3-89b.title: Trainer/Facilitator
getwingapp-getwingapp:lever:b06a6db3-89b.description: Trainer / Facilitator Company Description: Wing helps small businesses, startups, executives, and enterprises streamline their operations by providing access to top-tier remote talent. Role Summary: You’ll run classes and training sessions; assess competency; and loop feedback between Instructional Design and QA/OPS to keep content sharp.
responsibilities: New-hire onboarding for Virtual Assistants: run daily Google Meet classes covering Wing policies, professionalism, data privacy, security, time-tracking, and client etiquette.
Tool bootcamps: live demos and walkthroughs for common client tools: Calendly, Calendar, Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, ClickUp/Asana, CRM basics, Notion/Airtable; assign hands-on tasks etc.
Client-readiness drills: email/chat tone practice, communication style, meeting notes, task intake, follow-ups, and escalation paths; use Wing examples and templates.
SOP to action: translate client SOPs into step-by-step checklists; run simulated tickets/requests and score with a rubric.
Quality calibration with QA: score sample work, align standards (accuracy, turnaround time, formatting), and brief VAs on common defects.
Professionalism & reliability: coach punctuality, shift handover, calendar hygiene, status updates, and expectation setting with clients.
Systems compliance: verify VA setup (internet speed, power backup plan, headset/cam, workspace), security (2FA, password manager), and confidentiality acknowledgments.
LMS progression: enroll cohorts, gate modules, check completion, and remediate gaps before client endorsement.
Readiness sign-off: run quick quizzes and practicals; record scores; issue pass/hold with clear action items and deadlines.
Account-specific enablement: coordinate with OPS/Future SMEs to deliver short modules on client tools, workflows, and KPIs before deployment.
Performance follow-through: host week-1 and week-2 check-ins post-deployment; review QA feedback and schedule refreshers as needed.
Reporting: send weekly cohort report (attendance, pass rates, readiness risks, remediation plan) and track time-to-productivity metrics.
Feedback loop to instructional design: log confusing content, missing steps, or outdated screenshots; propose fixes and retest after updates.
qualifications: 2–4+ years in live training/facilitation, L&D, BPO coaching, or training enablement
Experience with assessing trainees, bridging gaps between instructional design and operational issues like Churn/escalation types
Clear, confident communicator; English neutral accent and strong pacing
Skilled at group management, cold-calling participants, and keeping sessions engaging
Comfortable with LMS (Thinkific or similar), Google Workspace, Zoom/Meet tools
Can assess performance with rubrics, give actionable feedback, and document results
Organized and reliable across time zones; thrives in fast iterations
